text: Soft US growth and caution on margin trajectory do not derail company turnaround; Reiterate Buy

Nestlé reported Q2 organic sales growth of 3.7% with +1.8% in RIG which, although in line with consensus, appeared light in the context of the stock's strong run into the print. Within group RIG, we flag the strong performance in AOA, with China yet to contribute. However, North America RIG in Q2 was -0.6% affected by destocking in Petcare and low consumer confidence weighing on performance. Europe RIG of +0.5% in Q2 was held back by delistings which might impact Q3 alongside the ongoing, albeit moderating, drag from the IMF recall. UTOP margin of 16.4% was better than expected despite an increase in marketing, but saw a 30bps one-off benefit from the pension scheme change.
Guidance unchanged but concerns remain around margins;

Management is expecting H2 UTOP margin to be similar to H1, but as the pension benefit should not benefit H2, it implies a sequential underlying improvement. Despite a volatile input cost environment, management reiterated its 17% mid-term guidance and committed to some margin progression in FY27e albeit not quantified at this stage. We forecast 20bps margin progression per year, assuming that any windfall will be reinvested in marketing to boost future RIG.
Progress on disposals could lead to a share buy back

announcement in 2027; Nestlé has announced plans to create a 50:50 JV with Platinum Equity, for its waters and premium beverages by H1 27. Nestlé expects to receive CHF2.8bn in cash proceeds at closing. Nestlé will also classify its mainstream VMS and ice cream businesses as “assets held for sale” as the sales processes progress.

Turnaround story will not be linear but still intact; While H1 is a set back and H2 is lapping tougher comps on RIG, we continue to see encouraging momentum in Petcare sell-out and resilience in coffee. We expect +1.1% RIG growth in Q3, +1.3% in Q4 and +1.9% in FY27e, close to the 2% target. Nestlé trades on an attractive 16x CY27e P/E with 5% FCF and 4% dividend yield.

text: We highlight the key positives and negatives from H1, starting with positive fundamentals for Petcare, strong growth in AOA (Asia, Oceania, Africa) and strong returns from cost savings;

I. The Pet food category shows good underlying fundamentals, despite temporary headwinds in the US in Q2 linked to destocking. Management remains confident in the category's medium-term growth outlook. By region, Petcare grew mid-single digit in Europe, while EMs demonstrated good momentum. However, growth was negatively affected by retailer inventory reductions in the US, which was likely caused by the company's improved supply levels reducing the need for retailers to hold onto safety stocks. Management confirmed that US sell-out trends remained strong in Q2 vs Q1, with an acceleration in cat food. Looking forward, Nestlé does not expect further impacts from retailer destocking but cautioned that Q4 growth will be lapping a tougher comp as Q4 25 Petcare sales benefitted from pre-buying ahead of planned price increases.

text: II. AOA's strong growth in Q2 was broad-based, with headwinds from Greater China easing as the trade inventory reductions were lower than Q1 25. Management called out strong growth in Japan and India, and confirmed that although India will begin to lap the tailwinds from GST changes in Q3, it continues to expect double-digit growth. In Greater China, the new management team is focusing on driving innovation, using the right distribution mechanisms, and prioritising the right brand investments. However, Nestlé's end-categories continue to decline -1% to -3%, and management acknowledged that for now it is still losing share in some categories. Excluding China, Nestlé has been consistently gaining share across AOA.

Cost savings investments already yielding strong returns, with savings coming in slightly ahead of plan and driving a 150bp benefit to margins in H1, through CHF600m in incremental procurement and operational efficiency savings. This brings cumulative savings from the Fuel for Growth program to CHF1.7bn putting Nestlé on-track to reach its CHF2bn ambition in FY26 and CHF3bn by the end of FY28. Cost savings are also supporting increased advertising and marketing spend which reached 8.9% in H2 vs H1 26, with the incremental spend targeted at the group's growth platforms.

text: We see the main negatives from H1 results as the lack of UTOP margin improvement now expected for H2 driving uncertainty around how much margins can expand in FY27, alongside continued headwinds from infant formula...

I. H2 margins are now only expected to be similar to H1 (previously guided for expansion HoH), with management confirming that improving raw material costs for coffee and cocoa are now likely to be at least partially offset by higher transport and energy costs due to the Middle East conflict. While management did confirm that Nestlé's UTOP margin is expected to improve further in FY27, albeit not quantified. Although the H1 26 UTOP margin of 16.4% includes a one-time +30bps benefit, it also includes operating deleverage associated with the infant formula recall (which should mostly normalise by the end of the year) and +40bps in higher marketing costs.

Nestlé's H1 UTOP margin had a one-time 30bps benefit from pension credits. This was due to a curtailment gain arising from Nestlé adjusting its benefits package to better align with employee preferences, by allowing employees to take a lump sum on retirement instead of only offering a regular pension payment. While management does not anticipate a further P&L benefit from these actions, they should provide a small cash flow benefit over time. Our understanding is that it won't benefit H2 26 but will be in the base for H1 27.

text: II. Infant formula remained a headwind to growth in Q2, despite the initial impact from the recall in Q1 subsiding. However, there was a clear sequential improvement, with infant nutrition sales down mid-teens in Q1, while in Q2 the decline was only mid-single digit. Nestlé expects further improvement throughout the rest of 2026 and for the business to have largely recovered by the end of the year.

III. Mixed bag in coffee with strong Americas and AOA offset by Europe weakness. US coffee RIG slowed as the group increased prices on its Starbucks portfolio, and saw a negative initial RIG reaction, as expected. However, in the rest of Zone Americas RIG strengthened, with double-digit growth in Nescafé across major markets, albeit with Coffee mate declining. AOA and Europe both saw RIG led high-single-digit growth led by Nescafé, as pricing moderated. In Nespresso, the group is seeing new and younger consumers entering the category, and is seeing share gains in the US with Vertuo, albeit with growth moderating. However, Europe remains under pressure driven by the ongoing competitive intensity in its Original line.

text: Progress on disposals with waters JV, and strong cash generation

Nestlé is progressing with its disposals, and has announced plans to create Peranel, a 50:50 JV with Platinum Equity, for Nestlé's waters and premium beverages. The transaction is expected to close in H1 27 and assigns an enterprise value of €4.9bn, implying Nestlé will receive CHF 2.8bn in cash proceeds at closing. Nestlé will also classify its mainstream VMS and ice cream businesses as “assets held for sale” as the sales processes progress. On a pro-forma basis, accounting for the waters proceeds, Nestlé would have CHF5.3bn available for debt reduction in FY27 and could reduce net debt to EBITDA to 2.3x (current GSe 2.5x). We expect Nestlé to deliver CHF 9.9bn FCF in FY26e, supported by lower capex and working capital efficiencies, with FCF generation H2 weighted.

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.
